items.summary: GPU tile_fft for non-power-of-two sizes on HIP: without libmathdx the GPU path supports only power-of-two sizes divisible by block_dim and raises ValueError otherwise (builtins.py:13435-13448); ROCm has no device-callable FFT, so closing the gap means an in-tree Bluestein or direct-DFT path upstream does not have

decided.note: 2026-11-18: defer, ship upstream's no-libmathdx behaviour in 1.14.0+rocm.0 and name the gap in the release notes

items.summary: Conditional graph nodes on HIP: capture_if/capture_while inside a graph capture need cudaGraphAddNode conditional nodes (CUDA 12.4+), which HIP 7.14 does not have; the port reports them unsupported as upstream does for older CUDA. Adopt native HIP conditional nodes if ROCm ever ships them

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report unsupported on HIP exactly as upstream does for old CUDA; HIP's plans are unknown and it may be a hardware limitation, so not expected soon

items.summary: Clang/LLVM GPU compiler options on HIP: wp.config.llvm_cuda (kernels JIT-compiled by the bundled Clang/LLVM instead of the vendor runtime compiler) and the --clang-build-toolchain build option are NVPTX-only; the bundled LLVM has no AMDGPU target. The port makes both fail with a clear error on HIP. Supporting them would mean building and shipping LLVM with the AMDGPU backend and ROCm device libraries; hipRTC is already Clang-based, so there is no known AMD use case

decided.note: 2026-11-18: do not port it in this line, and make both switches fail clearly instead of misbehaving

items.summary: rocPRIM 4.8 (ROCm 10.2 rocm-sdk wheels), gfx950: hipcub::DeviceRadixSort::SortKeys on uint64_t keys returns output that is not sorted by the selected bits when end_bit == 64 and begin_bit > 0 (tested 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 31, 32, 33, 40) for more than 1024 keys; [0,64), [0,63), [1,63), [16,48), [32,56), [32,63) are correct. cuBQL's GPU builders sort {primID,nodeID} with bits [32,64), so leaves with several primitives were built wrong (Warp test_mesh_query_ray_count_intersections, cubql leaf size 4, 1337/5000 rays). Port works around it by sorting [0,64) under __HIPCC__ in the vendored sah_builder.h; sm_builder.h, elh_builder.h and rebinMortonBuilder.h (not used by Warp) have the same [32,64) sort, and upstream cuBQL's HIP path is affected too

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; standalone reproducer and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), 2x gfx942: a captured hipMemcpyAsync between pinned host memory and memory allocated in the same capture (hipMallocAsync) makes hipGraphInstantiateWithFlags return hipErrorNotSupported (801) unless the capture device is 0 and the pinned buffer was allocated with device 0 current (D2H also works when both are device 1); on capture device 0 with the pinned buffer allocated on device 1, H2D segfaults the process. items.summary: AMD clang 24 (ROCm 10.2 wheels, hipRTC and offline -O3), gfx950: when one function computes __fsqrt_rn(x) (llvm.sqrt.f32 with !fpmath 3.0, the approximate native sqrt) and sqrtf(x) (llvm.sqrt.f32 without !fpmath, correctly rounded) of the same value, EarlyCSE merges the two calls and keeps the !fpmath tag, so sqrtf becomes the approximation: 2535452 of the 16777216 floats in [1,4) off by 1 ulp, against 0 when sqrtf is alone or at -O0. The merged call should drop !fpmath (the most generic of the two). Seen through a Warp user snippet that used both; Warp's own wp.sqrt is unaffected unless a snippet in the same function uses __fsqrt_rn. Standalone reproducer sq3.hip in the notes; not checked against upstream LLVM main

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; reproducer confirmed on current ROCm and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx1100 (W7800): hipDrvMemcpy3DAsync and the runtime hipMemcpy3DAsync from pageable (malloc) host memory into a hipArray still read the host buffer after the call returns: overwriting the buffer right after the call and then synchronizing leaves every element of the array with the overwritten value (1D w=32/256/4096, 2D 2x2/64x64/1024x1024; runtime API 2048 of 2048 wrong). Linear hipMemcpyAsync H2D stages pageable memory correctly (0 bad). CUDA stages pageable memory before an async copy returns, and Warp relies on that: textures built from NumPy data had their first 16 bytes replaced by glibc free-list pointers once the temporary host copy was freed. Warp now synchronizes the stream after a host-side 3D copy outside a capture. Reproducer m3d_pageable.cpp in the notes
refs: projects/warp-1.14/notes.md (Evidence session 2 linux-gfx1100, Finding 2; Porting session 6)

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; reproducer confirmed on current ROCm and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx1100 (W7800): hipDrvMemcpy3DAsync on a stream capturing in global mode returns success but copies immediately and adds no node to the graph (device->array->device: graph has 0 nodes, the copy has happened before instantiation, a replay after changing the source copies nothing, 2048 of 2048 wrong). items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), Windows, gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S); also in rocm-systems develop: with no direct dispatch (the Windows default, 'Direct Dispatch: 0'), GraphExec::Run for a graph instantiated with hipGraphInstantiateFlagAutoFreeOnLaunch calls FreeAllMemory() and resets memalloc_nodes_ on the launching thread before launch_stream->finish(), while the worker thread may still run the previous launch's VirtualMemFreeNode::submit (allocation executed, kernel still running). The worker then frees memory the pool no longer owns ('Memory didn't belong to any pool!', hip_graph_internal.hpp:3823), memalloc_nodes_ underflows, and the next launches either return hipErrorInvalidValue from the repeat-launch check or crash with an access violation in amdhip64_7.dll + 0x160C6C on the worker thread. Standalone reproducer graph_autofree_race.hip (hipMallocAsync, 2 ms kernel, hipFreeAsync captured; 10 back-to-back launches) crashes on launch 2; synchronizing the stream before each hipGraphLaunch passes. Seen through Warp test_mesh_refit_graph (crash) and test_grouped_capture_bvh_rebuild (invalid argument). Warp now synchronizes before hipGraphLaunch on Windows (hip_compat.h). Fix would be to finish the stream (or wait for the previous launch) before FreeAllMemory, and make memalloc_nodes_ atomic

HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), Windows, gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S); same code in rocm-systems develop: with no direct dispatch (the Windows default), a graph memory allocation node maps its allocation in GraphMemAllocNode::VirtualMemAllocNode::submit on the worker thread (first launch, and by reading every launch of an AutoFreeOnLaunch exec, since GraphExec::Run calls ReleaseCachedMapping which clears mapped_). submit calls amd::MemObjMap::RemoveMemObj on the reserved VA (registered by CreateCommand on the launching thread), then AllocateMemory and only then maps and registers the sub-object. Two consequences. (1) A call on another thread that validates a pointer into the allocation inside that window returns hipErrorInvalidValue: reproducer graph_alloc_first_launch.hip (capture hipMallocAsync + kernel, no free, AutoFreeOnLaunch, launch, hipMemcpyAsync 4 KiB D2H right after hipGraphLaunch) fails 5 of 5 at 1 MiB and 256 MiB; seen through Warp test_cuda_graph_alloc_transient_stream and test_map test_graph_capture; Warp now synchronizes after hipGraphLaunch on Windows (hip_compat.h). (2) Inside hipGraphLaunch: GraphMemsetNode::CreateCommand (launching thread) looks up its destination with getMemoryObjectForCurrentDevice WITHOUT WorkerThreadLock_ (GraphMemcpyNode1D::CreateCommand takes it around the same lookup, and submit holds it across the window), returns hipErrorInvalidValue, and the launch fails with 'Command creation for node id(N) failed!'. Reproducer graph_memset_first_launch.hip (two root branches: hipMallocAsync+hipMemsetAsync+kernel; hipMallocAsync+H2D hipMemcpyAsync; 1 MiB; one launch per process): 2 of 11 launches failed; without the memset node 0 of 21; under AMD_LOG_LEVEL=1 0 of 20. Seen through Warp test_cuda_graph_alloc_transient_stream (node id(3) = memset of the first allocation in Kahn launch order) and test_graph_alloc (single-stream: alloc 512 B, memset, kernels; 2 of 6 test_graph runs), and after such a failed launch the next Warp test hung. Fix: take WorkerThreadLock_ in GraphMemsetNode::CreateCommand like the memcpy node, and/or keep the VA registered (replace the entry atomically) while the alloc node maps physical memory. Warp skips test_cuda_graph_alloc_transient_stream on Windows HIP (9d9a6161).

summary_history.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), Windows, gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S); same code in rocm-systems develop: with no direct dispatch (the Windows default), the first launch of a graph holding a memory allocation node runs GraphMemAllocNode::VirtualMemAllocNode::submit on the worker thread, which calls amd::MemObjMap::RemoveMemObj on the reserved VA (registered by CreateCommand on the launching thread), then AllocateMemory (milliseconds for large sizes) and only then maps and registers the sub-object. A call on another thread that validates a pointer into the allocation inside that window returns hipErrorInvalidValue. Standalone reproducer graph_alloc_first_launch.hip (capture hipMallocAsync + kernel, no free, instantiate with AutoFreeOnLaunch, launch once, hipMemcpyAsync 4 KiB D2H on the same stream right after hipGraphLaunch returns) fails 5 of 5 at 1 MiB and 256 MiB; hipStreamSynchronize after the launch passes. Seen through Warp test_graph test_cuda_graph_alloc_transient_stream and test_map test_graph_capture (wp_memcpy_d2h invalid argument after wp.capture_launch). A rarer variant fails inside hipGraphLaunch itself ('Command creation for node id(3) failed!', hipErrorInvalidValue) on a 2-stream graph, consistent with the launching thread validating a memcpy node's pointer while another worker is inside that allocation's window; not reproduced standalone. Warp now synchronizes after hipGraphLaunch on Windows (hip_compat.h). Fix would be to keep the VA registered (or replace the entry atomically) while the alloc node maps physical memory
summary_history.reason: session 16 identified and reproduced the in-launch variant: it is the memset node's unlocked lookup, not the memcpy node (which holds WorkerThreadLock_), and it also hits single-stream graphs and AutoFreeOnLaunch relaunches

items.summary: On the gfx1250 fleet device (a0 revision) ROCm 10.2's load-time code-object translator (libhsa_hotswap_rocjitsu) fails or mistranslates three Warp kernels: s_set_pc_i64 'indirect branch or call target recovery is not implemented' (module load fails, HIP 209), the built-in radix sort kernel not loading (209), and wrong mesh_query_point results after 'synthesized s_endpgm boundary' warnings. Reproducer: python -m warp.tests -s autodetect -p test_fem_geometry.py.

HIP's GL interop on Linux finds Mesa's GLX interop entry points with dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT), so hipGraphicsGLRegisterBuffer/Image fail with hipErrorInvalidValue when the application loaded libGL with RTLD_LOCAL (Python ctypes, pyglet), and the failed lookup is cached for the process; also HIP has no EGL path, so headless contexts can never register.
